clio — clio 0.1.0

Usage:
  clio version
       Print package identity
  clio health
       Machine-readable health/version JSON
  clio mcp schema-export [--out FILE] [--path FILE]
       Print/write the tool_schema pack (alias: --path)
  clio mcp stdio [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                 [--bank BANK]
       Run the MCP stdio transport
  clio mcp http [--bind [ADDR]] [--db PATH]
                [--backend sqlite|postgres] [--bank BANK] [--token-file PATH]
                [--sessions] [--insecure-no-auth] [--insecure-bind-any]
       Run the MCP Streamable HTTP transport; with no flag (or a bare --bind) scan
       127.0.0.1:34300-34309 for the first free port; an explicit HOST:PORT binds exactly that
       address
  clio ops diagnose [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                    [--bank BANK]
       Read-only install/database health snapshot
  clio ops verify [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                  [--bank BANK]
       Referential-integrity and index-coverage checks
  clio ops doctor [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                  [--bank BANK] [--dry-run false]
       Compose a repair plan (read-only)
  clio ops repair [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                  [--bank BANK] [--plan PLAN_ID] [--actions a,b] [--confirm]
       Apply allowlisted repairs (live run requires --confirm)
  clio ops reindex [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                   [--bank BANK] [--target dense|lexical|all] [--dry-run]
                   [--confirm]
       Rebuild derived indexes (live run requires --confirm); `--dry-run` is report-only and
       applies nothing, so a report-only run is not reported as ok. A lexical rebuild
       replaces legacy plaintext index rows with keyed term digests. Ops exit codes: 0
       healthy or completed, 1 domain/runtime failure or findings, 2 usage or repair
       refusal, 3 reindex failed or ran report-only
  clio status [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres] [--dir DIR]
              [--output json|text]
       Read-only unified stack health (setup, database, listeners, Compose, diagnose). Exit
       codes: 0 healthy, 1 degraded, 2 usage
  clio compose up [--dir DIR] [--services LIST]
       Materialize the compose stack and start the local Docker services (postgres, embed,
       rerank, extract)
  clio compose down [--dir DIR] [--services LIST]
       Stop and remove the services `clio compose up` started; re-runnable
  clio setup [--database managed|sqlite|existing] [--config PATH]
             [--db-path PATH] [--database-url ADDRESS]
             [--database-connect pasted|typed] [--database-host H]
             [--database-port P] [--database-name N] [--database-user U]
             [--database-password P] [--database-ssl MODE]
             [--database-ssl-rootcert PATH] [--database-option NAME=VALUE]...
             [--embed local|online] [--embed-url U] [--embed-model M]
             [--embed-key K] [--embed-provider tei|openai] [--embed-dims N]
             [--rerank local|online|skip] [--rerank-url U] [--rerank-model M]
             [--rerank-key K] [--rerank-provider tei|cohere]
             [--extract local|skip|online] [--compose-dir DIR]
             [--key-store file|keystore] [--sync-store file|keystore]
             [--allow-untested] [--yes] [--non-interactive] [--interactive]
       Configure the stack and write the deployment config the binary reads (see `clio setup
       --help` for the full flag set)
  clio retention schema
       Print the retention profile JSON Schema
  clio retention get [--bank BANK] [--profiles FILE]
       Show the effective per-bank retention profile
  clio retention set [--bank BANK] [--scope bank|deployment]
                     --profile JSON [--profile-file FILE] [--profiles FILE]
       Store a validated retention profile (persists to --profiles/env)
  clio compliance inventory [--output json|text]
       Read the stored record families and known copies: one row per family with its source,
       subject link or named gap, custody, and retention action; open rows stay open and
       named, declared caller copies are recorded and never touched, and nothing is written
  clio compliance review-export --out FILE [--limit N]
                                [--cursor C] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                                [--output json|text]
       Write the ordered local review events to a content-free file under destination
       custody (requires --actor harness|system)
  clio compliance request-start --request-id ID
                                --kind copy|erasure [--subject-id SUBJECT]
                                [--verification verified|unverified]
                                [--deadline TIME] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                                [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_start
       Open one durable subject request, or replay the stored one of the same id, and report
       its separated status
  clio compliance request-status --request-id ID
                                 [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_status
       Report one durable request's state, technical completion, pending operator actions,
       and outcome as separate fields
  clio compliance request-retry --request-id ID
                                --subject-id SUBJECT --legal-basis BASIS
                                [--reason-code CODE] [--confirm] [--bank BANK]
                                [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_retry
       Retry a confirmed erasure through its durable request id and report the pending
       action and effect counts
  clio compliance request-copy --copy-id ID
                               --request-id ID --custody CLASS
                               --owner harness|system
                               --required-action erase|remove|delivery|notice
                               --state STATE [--exception-reason REASON]
                               [--updated-at TIME] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                               [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_copy
       Record one copy-inventory disposition for a request and report the request
  clio compliance request-exception
                                    --request-id ID --reason REASON [--bank BANK]
                                    [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_exception
       Record a request-level retention exception and report the request
  clio compliance request-events --request-id ID
                                 [--limit N] [--cursor C] [--bank BANK]
                                 [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_events
       Read one content-free page of the local events bound to one request
  clio compliance request-path-complete
                                        --request-id ID --product-path PATH
                                        [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                                        [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_path_complete
       Record a verified product-path result (requires --actor harness|system)
  clio compliance request-close --request-id ID
                                --product-path PATH [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                                [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_close
       Accept closure for one request, finalize its outcome, and report the request
  clio compliance peer-status --request-id ID
                              [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_peer_status
       Report the derived peer state slots of one request from its durable per-peer rows
  clio compliance peer-retry --request-id ID
                             [--legal-basis BASIS] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                             [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_peer_retry
       Reconcile the pending erasure actions a restart left on one request and report it
  clio compliance peer-disposition --request-id ID
                                   --peer-id PEER --disposition DISPOSITION
                                   [--proof-ref REF] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                                   [--output json|text]   -> subject_request_peer_disposition
       Record one peer disposition for a request and report the request and its peer states
  clio recall QUERY [--bank BANK] [--limit N] [--domains a,b]
              [--as-of TS] [--query-anchor TS] [--time-axis valid|transaction]
              [--min-semantic N] [--min-keyword N] [--min-reranker N]
              [--min-final N] [--no-entities] [--entity-summary]
              [--output json|text]   -> retrieve
       score floors are relative filters over this query's own scores, not calibrated
       thresholds
  clio get ID [--snapshot|--gist] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> get
       fetch one memory by id
  clio show ID [--snapshot|--gist] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> get
       alias of `get`
  clio inspect [--filter JSON] [--category C] [--epistemic-kind K]
               [--validity V] [--time-start TS] [--time-end TS] [--limit N]
               [--offset N] [--include-discarded] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> inspect
       metadata-only listing, no decrypted body
  clio stats [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> stats
       count memories, entities, and index state in one bank
  clio task get TASK_ID [--explain] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> task_get
       one task and its current state
  clio task history TASK_ID [--limit N] [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                    [--output json|text]   -> task_history
       a task's recorded transitions
  clio failure list TASK_ID_OR_QUERY [--limit N] [--explain]
                    [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> failures_for_task
       failures recorded against one task
  clio memtree query [--time-start TS] [--time-end TS]
                     [--task-id ID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--explain]
                     [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> memtree_query
       walk the memory tree from a seed
  clio memtree get NODE_ID [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> memtree_get
       one memory-tree node and its lineage
  clio history temporal TARGET [--as-of TS]
                        [--time-axis valid|transaction] [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                        [--output json|text]   -> temporal_history
       the item history as it stood at a point in time
  clio triple query [SUBJECT [PREDICATE [OBJECT]]] [--subject S]
                    [--predicate P] [--object O] [--as-of TS]
                    [--time-axis valid|transaction] [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                    [--output json|text]   -> triple_query
       match subject/predicate/object patterns
  clio belief history BELIEF_ID_OR_PROPOSITION [--explain]
                      [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> belief_history
       one belief's confidence history
  clio graph query SEED_ID [--max-hops N]
                   [--edge-type coactivation|explicit] [--min-weight W] [--explain]
                   [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> graph_query
       neighbours of one item, by edge type
  clio associations ITEM_ID [--min-weight W] [--explain]
                    [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> associations
       co-activation links for one item
  clio persona get [--budget-tokens N] [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> persona_get
       the persona model, within a token budget
  clio persona stable KEY VALUE [--confidence N]
                      [--source explicit|inferred] [--evidence-ref E]
                      [--context TEXT] [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
                      [--output json|text]   -> persona_put_stable
       set a stable persona key
  clio persona observe KEY NUMBER [--confidence N]
                       [--source explicit|inferred] [--evidence-ref E] [--bank BANK]
                       [--output json|text]   -> persona_observe_preference
       feed one numeric observation into the EMA
  clio task upsert TASK_ID --definition D --status S [--steps a,b]
                   [--evidence-ref E] [--context TEXT] [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> task_upsert
       create or update one task
  clio failure record TASK_ID --attempt-n N --what-failed W
                      --lesson L [--evidence-ref E] [--context TEXT] [--dry-run]
                      [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> failure_record
       record one attempt, its failure, and the lesson
  clio scratchpad write KEY CONTENT [--session S]
                        [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> scratchpad_write
       store an ephemeral key for this session
  clio scratchpad read [KEY] [--session S] [--bank BANK]
                       [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> scratchpad_read
       read one key, or the whole pad
  clio scratchpad clear [KEY] [--session S] [--bank BANK]
                        [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> scratchpad_clear
       drop one key, or the whole pad
  clio canonical put KEY VALUE --category C --epistemic-kind K
                     [--source-type T] [--confidence N] [--source-text TEXT]
                     [--evidence-ref E] [--context C] [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
                     [--output json|text]   -> canonical_put
       gated single-slot upsert with bi-temporal supersession
  clio canonical get KEY [--as-of TS] [--bank BANK]
                     [--output json|text]   -> canonical_get
       read one canonical key
  clio shared store TEXT --epistemic-kind K [--category C]
                    [--episodic-type T] [--source-type T] [--confidence N]
                    [--evidence-ref E] --actor ACTOR --shared-bank
                    [--output json|text]   -> shared_store
       write into a shared bank
  clio shared retrieve QUERY --actor ACTOR --shared-bank
                       [--output json|text]   -> shared_retrieve
       read from a shared bank
  clio shared discard ITEM_ID --reason R [--confirm]
                      --actor ACTOR --shared-bank [--output json|text]   -> shared_discard
       remove one item from a shared bank
  clio validate ITEM_ID --action attest|update|invalidate|delete
                [--note N] [--new-content C] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                [--output json|text]   -> validate
       attest, update, invalidate, or delete one item
  clio batch --file ops.json [--dry-run] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
             [--output json|text]   -> batch
       apply a list of operations in one transaction
  clio maintenance status [--item-id ID] [--explain]
                          [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> maintenance_status
       queue depth, failures, and drain progress
  clio intent gate TURN_TEXT [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> intent_gate
       decide whether a turn should reach memory
  clio compose-context [QUERY] --budget-tokens N
                       [--domains a,b] [--as-of TS] [--query-anchor TS]
                       [--time-axis valid|transaction]
                       [--recall-scope full|consolidated_only] [--expand-graph]
                       [--prefer-consolidated] [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                       [--output json|text]   -> compose_context
       assemble a budgeted context block for a turn
  clio audit trail ITEM_ID [--explain] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> audit_trail
       masked lifecycle reconstruction for one item
  clio hygiene audit [--min-score N] [--limit N] [--offset N]
                     [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> hygiene_audit
       score stored items and list the weakest
  clio hygiene clean --file candidates.json
                     [--action flag|archive|discard|keep] [--confirm] [--dry-run]
                     [--reason R] [--note N] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> hygiene_clean
       (or --file - for stdin; without --confirm, or with --dry-run: zero-write dry-run
       only)
  clio hygiene log [--limit N] [--offset N] [--bank BANK]
                   [--output json|text]   -> hygiene_log_list
       what hygiene has already done
  clio export --out FILE
              [--content-mode dsar_plaintext|ciphertext_backup] [--category C]
              [--time-start TS] [--time-end TS] [--include-archived true|false]
              [--include-discarded true|false] [--subject S] [--bank BANK]
              [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> export
       (manifest-backed JSON bundle; requires --actor harness|system)
  clio import --source FILE [--dry-run] [--force] [--reason R]
              [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> import
       load a bundle produced by `clio export`
  clio erase --subject S --basis B --request R [--reason-code C]
             --confirm [--actor harness|system] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> erase_request
       IRREVERSIBLE compliance erasure (DEK destruction); distinct from `discard` and
       hygiene cleanup
  clio remember TEXT --category C [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
                [--epistemic-kind fact|belief] [--confidence N] [--source-type T]
                [--evidence-ref E] [--context TEXT] [--allow-duplicate] [--dry-run]
                [--output json|text]   -> store
  clio admit TEXT --category C [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR]
             [--epistemic-kind fact|belief] [--confidence N] [--source-type T]
             [--evidence-ref E] [--context TEXT] [--output json|text]   -> admit_preview
       score one write without storing it; `--file ops.json` previews a whole batch instead
  clio summarize --scope S [--dry-run] [--output json|text]   -> summarize
       summarize one scope into a consolidated unit
  clio consolidate [--bank BANK] [--force] [--dry-run]
                   [--output json|text]   -> consolidate
       run the consolidation wave over a bank
  clio update ID VALUE --rule discrete|continuous [--dry-run]
              [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> update
       set an item's value under a named rule
  clio invalidate ID [--replacement ID] [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
                  [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> invalidate
       close an item's validity; never deletes
  clio discard ID --reason R --confirm [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
               [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> discard
       operational removal; distinct from compliance erasure
  clio correct ID VALUE --reason R [--context TEXT] [--confirm]
               [--dry-run] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]   -> correct
       replace an item's value with a stated reason
  clio triple add S P O [--epistemic-kind fact|belief]
                  [--source-type T] [--confidence N] [--context TEXT]
                  [--valid-from TS] [--valid-until TS] [--supersede true|false]
                  [--subject-id ID] [--update-rule discrete] [--dry-run]
                  [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> triple_add
       write one subject/predicate/object fact
  clio triple end S P [--object O] --valid-until TS
                  [--update-rule discrete] [--dry-run] [--bank BANK]
                  [--output json|text]   -> triple_end
       close an open fact without a replacement
  clio belief observe PROP --confidence C --evidence E
                      --source S [--as-of TS] [--subject-id ID] [--context TEXT]
                      [--dry-run] [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> belief_observe
       record evidence and a new confidence
  clio graph link A B --relationship R [--weight W] [--dry-run]
                  [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]   -> graph_link
       add an explicit edge between two items
  clio config get [PATH] [--output json|text]   -> config_get
       read one configuration path
  clio config set PATH VALUE [--scope session|profile|deployment]
                  [--output json|text]   -> config_set
       write one configuration path at a scope
  clio config profiles [--output json|text]   -> config_profiles
       list the available configuration profiles
  clio config use NAME [--output json|text]   -> config_profile_apply
       apply one profile by name
  clio ranking get [--output json|text]   -> ranking_env_get
       read the ranking environment
  clio ranking set --patch JSON [--patch-file FILE] [--dry-run]
                   [--output json|text]   -> ranking_env_set
       patch the ranking environment
  clio sync status [--banks a,b] [--output json|text]   -> sync_status
       explain what sync would do, and omit when disabled
  clio sync push --remote HOST:PORT [--mode push|pull|bidirectional]
                 [--banks a,b] [--token T] [--output json|text]   -> sync_push
       send local changes to a sync server
  clio sync pull --remote HOST:PORT [--mode push|pull|bidirectional]
                 [--banks a,b] [--token T] [--output json|text]   -> sync_pull
       take remote changes from a sync server
  clio sync serve [--bind ADDR] [--banks a,b] [--token-file PATH]
                  [--ttl-secs N] [--dev] [--output json|text]   -> sync_serve
       run the sync server in the foreground
  clio sync keygen [--store file|keystore] [--output json|text]
       Create the sync key in the recorded store and record the choice; the key is printed
       exactly once and cannot be recovered except with `clio sync key export`
  clio sync key export [--output json|text]
       Print the stored sync key; a shell flag or environment variable leaves the key in
       process listings, so a shared deployment should point CLIO_SYNC_KEY_FILE at an
       owner-only key file
  clio sync key status [--output json|text]   -> sync_key_status
       Show the sync key's store, fingerprint, creation time, and count; never the key
  clio backup dir [--output json|text]
       Show and create the backup directory (no database needed)
  clio backup create [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres]
                     [--label TEXT] [--note TEXT] [--keep N] [--confirm] [--dry-run]
                     [--output json|text]
       Snapshot the store into one owner-only archive: a SQLite store is a compacted,
       transactionally consistent copy (one VACUUM INTO, logically equivalent, never a
       byte-for-byte clone, and it does not retain deleted pages); a Postgres store is a
       row-level dump in COPY text format, whose schema is owned by this build; --keep N
       then prunes the backup directory to the newest N (nothing without --confirm); exit 3
       means pruning could not remove every candidate
  clio backup list [--limit N] [--output json|text]
       List snapshots newest first by manifest time (no database needed); --db and --backend
       are refused because they cannot change the listing
  clio backup prune --keep N [--confirm] [--dry-run]
                    [--output json|text]
       Delete all but the newest N snapshots by manifest time: the newest snapshot is never
       deleted, an unreadable archive is reported and kept, and without --confirm nothing is
       removed. Exit codes: 0 report-only or complete prune, 3 confirmed prune could not
       remove every candidate
  clio backup restore ID | clio backup restore --latest [--yes]
                      [--no-input] [--no-pre-backup] [--allow-missing-keys]
                      [--dry-run] [--output json|text]
       Replace the selected store with the archive (never a merge); a pre-restore snapshot
       is taken first unless --no-pre-backup; for a SQLite store the swap removes the
       target's write-ahead log before it renames the new store in, so a crash in that
       window loses whatever that log had not yet written; a Postgres restore replaces the
       target in one transaction and has no such window; --no-pre-backup is what leaves that
       window with no way back. Exit codes: 0 clean restore, 1 operational failure, 2
       refused, 3 partial or not-durable restore, 75 means the command could not report a
       clean success and that nothing was lost or invalid, and the command's own message
       says whether a retry helps: a storage lock conflict is cleared by retrying, and a
       restore that left a derived difference is not. Here that code is a restore that
       loaded every user-data row and differs in a table the store rebuilds; retrying it
       reloads the same archive and reproduces the same count, and the index pipeline
       reconciles it on its next pass
  clio backup verify ID | clio backup verify --latest
                     [--output json|text]
       Re-check one archive's digests and its payload's validity; --db and --backend are
       refused because they cannot change the verdict
  clio auth token add --label LABEL --actor ACTOR --bank BANK
                      [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]
       Generate a network credential, print its secret exactly once, and store only the
       digest in the owner-only token store; the secret cannot be recovered
  clio auth token list [--output json|text]
       Show labels, actors, banks, and created_at; never a secret or a digest
  clio auth token revoke --label LABEL [--output json|text]
       Remove the record; takes effect at the next server start
  clio install --harness <name>
       Register the clio MCP server with a supported agent harness (see `clio install
       --help` for the supported harnesses)
  clio uninstall --harness <name>
       Remove the clio MCP server registration from a supported agent harness (see `clio
       uninstall --help` for the supported harnesses)
  clio help [--json] [--markdown --out DIR] [TOPIC]
       Global flags: --db --backend --bank --actor --output (-o). Output mode: an explicit
       `--output`/`-o` always wins; otherwise text on a terminal (TTY) and JSON when piped.
       Forms: `--output json`, `--output=json`, `-o json`, `-o=json`. Empty values: a value
       flag given an empty value (`--bank ''`) is refused on every command; leave the flag
       off to take the default. Use -- after the command before positional text that starts
       with -; keep flags before it. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 domain or runtime failure, 2 usage
       error or documented command refusal (ops repair or backup restore), 3 is a
       command-specific degraded outcome (clio ops reindex, backup prune or backup create
       --keep, or backup restore). 75 means the command could not report a clean success and
       that nothing was lost or invalid, and the command's own message says whether a retry
       helps: a storage lock conflict is cleared by retrying, and a restore that left a
       derived difference is not. Process stops caused by SIGPIPE, SIGINT, or SIGTERM cannot
       report a CLI error; shells that use the 128+signal convention show these as 141, 130,
       or 143, outside the command exit codes


Database (no flags or config file needed):
  default:    /home/clio/.local/share/clio/clio.db  (backend: sqlite)
  precedence: --db > the config file > CLIO_DATABASE_URL > CLIO_DATA_DIR > XDG_DATA_HOME > HOME > ./clio.db
  env:        CLIO_DATA_DIR names the directory; the resolver appends clio.db
  empty:      a value flag given an empty value (--db '') is refused; leave the flag off to take the default

usage: clio backup restore ID | clio backup restore --latest [--yes] [--no-input] [--no-pre-backup] [--allow-missing-keys] [--dry-run] [--output json|text]
       replaces the selected store with the archive's, never a merge: the archive's database and key store overwrite the live ones, a SQLite restore swaps the archived database file in, and a Postgres restore replaces every row of the target in one transaction, so a failure halfway leaves the target untouched. A pre-restore snapshot of the current store is taken first by default; --no-pre-backup skips it and says so. The swap of a SQLite store clears the target's write-ahead log before it renames the new store in, so a crash in that window loses whatever the log had not yet written into the store; a Postgres restore replaces the target in one transaction and has no such window; that snapshot is the only thing that covers it, so --no-pre-backup accepts the window rather than removing it. The archive holds key material when it carries a key member, so keep it owner-only; --allow-missing-keys accepts an archive without one and the restored content is then permanently unreadable. On a terminal the snapshot id must be typed exactly; off one, --yes is required, and --no-input forces the non-interactive path

  --latest  Selects the newest snapshot instead of a positional id; `backup_cli::resolve_restore_id` resolves it.
  --yes  Answers the confirmation gate in `backup_restore_cli::confirm`, restoring without a typed snapshot id.
  --no-input  Forces the non-interactive path in `backup_restore_cli::confirm`, refusing rather than prompting.
  --no-pre-backup  Skips the pre-restore snapshot the restore backends take by default; that snapshot is the only way back.
  --allow-missing-keys  Accepts an archive with no key member; `backup_restore_flow::refuse_missing_keys` then restores content that stays permanently unreadable.
  --dry-run  Prints the restore plan through `backup_restore_flow::planned` and changes no store.

       List snapshots newest first by manifest time (no database needed); --db and --backend
       are refused because they cannot change the listing
  clio backup prune --keep N [--confirm] [--dry-run]
                    [--output json|text]
       Delete all but the newest N snapshots by manifest time: the newest snapshot is never
       deleted, an unreadable archive is reported and kept, and without --confirm nothing is
       removed. Exit codes: 0 report-only or complete prune, 3 confirmed prune could not
       remove every candidate
  clio backup restore ID | clio backup restore --latest [--yes]
                      [--no-input] [--no-pre-backup] [--allow-missing-keys]
                      [--dry-run] [--output json|text]
       Replace the selected store with the archive (never a merge); a pre-restore snapshot
       is taken first unless --no-pre-backup; for a SQLite store the swap removes the
       target's write-ahead log before it renames the new store in, so a crash in that
       window loses whatever that log had not yet written; a Postgres restore replaces the
       target in one transaction and has no such window; --no-pre-backup is what leaves that
       window with no way back. Exit codes: 0 clean restore, 1 operational failure, 2
       refused, 3 partial or not-durable restore, 75 means the command could not report a
       clean success and that nothing was lost or invalid, and the command's own message
       says whether a retry helps: a storage lock conflict is cleared by retrying, and a
       restore that left a derived difference is not. Here that code is a restore that
       loaded every user-data row and differs in a table the store rebuilds; retrying it
       reloads the same archive and reproduces the same count, and the index pipeline
       reconciles it on its next pass
  clio backup verify ID | clio backup verify --latest
                     [--output json|text]
       Re-check one archive's digests and its payload's validity; --db and --backend are
       refused because they cannot change the verdict
  clio auth token add --label LABEL --actor ACTOR --bank BANK
                      [--bank BANK] [--output json|text]
       Generate a network credential, print its secret exactly once, and store only the
       digest in the owner-only token store; the secret cannot be recovered
  clio auth token list [--output json|text]
       Show labels, actors, banks, and created_at; never a secret or a digest
  clio auth token revoke --label LABEL [--output json|text]
       Remove the record; takes effect at the next server start
  clio install --harness <name>
       Register the clio MCP server with a supported agent harness (see `clio install
       --help` for the supported harnesses)
  clio uninstall --harness <name>
       Remove the clio MCP server registration from a supported agent harness (see `clio
       uninstall --help` for the supported harnesses)
  clio help [--json] [--markdown --out DIR] [TOPIC]
       Global flags: --db --backend --bank --actor --output (-o). Output mode: an explicit
       `--output`/`-o` always wins; otherwise text on a terminal (TTY) and JSON when piped.
       Forms: `--output json`, `--output=json`, `-o json`, `-o=json`. Empty values: a value
       flag given an empty value (`--bank ''`) is refused on every command; leave the flag
       off to take the default. Use -- after the command before positional text that starts
       with -; keep flags before it. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 domain or runtime failure, 2 usage
       error or documented command refusal (ops repair or backup restore), 3 is a
       command-specific degraded outcome (clio ops reindex, backup prune or backup create
       --keep, or backup restore). 75 means the command could not report a clean success and
       that nothing was lost or invalid, and the command's own message says whether a retry
       helps: a storage lock conflict is cleared by retrying, and a restore that left a
       derived difference is not. Process stops caused by SIGPIPE, SIGINT, or SIGTERM cannot
       report a CLI error; shells that use the 128+signal convention show these as 141, 130,
       or 143, outside the command exit codes

clio mcp http [--bind [ADDR]] [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres] [--bank BANK] [--token-file PATH] [--sessions] [--insecure-no-auth] [--insecure-bind-any]

--bind ADDR  Bind address. With no flag, or with a bare `--bind`, scan 127.0.0.1:34300-34309
             for the first free port. An explicit `--bind HOST:PORT` binds exactly
             that address; a non-loopback address also requires a credential, or
             both --insecure-no-auth and --insecure-bind-any.

--token-file PATH
             Credential store whose records name an actor and the banks it may reach
             (see `clio auth token add`). Loaded once at start; a path that is
             absent, unreadable, malformed, or holds no record refuses the start.
             Required on every bind unless --insecure-no-auth is given; outside
             loopback that opt-out also needs --insecure-bind-any.

--insecure-no-auth
             Permit a bind with no credential. Without it a credential is
             required everywhere, including loopback: name a --token-file store,
             or the start is refused. A --token-file store, when given, is still
             enforced. It does not permit a non-loopback bind: that needs
             --insecure-bind-any as well.

--insecure-bind-any
             Permit --insecure-no-auth to bind a non-loopback address. The start
             then warns that every host that can reach the port can use every
             tool. Without it a non-loopback bind with no credential is refused
             even with --insecure-no-auth.

[--help]
Ask where your memories and your models should live, show a preview, then write
the deployment config the binary reads without any environment variable.

Database:
  managed   Clio runs Postgres in Docker on this machine only, no password
  sqlite    a SQLite file on this machine, no Docker
  existing  a Postgres that already exists; paste the address or type the fields

The managed database publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 and asks Postgres for trust
authentication, so it is unreachable off this machine and needs no password. Every
process on this machine can still reach it, which is the ordinary exposure of a local
development database. --database-password applies to the existing route only.
SSL modes: disable, prefer, verify-full, encrypt-no-verify. verify-full checks the
certificate and the server name. encrypt-no-verify encrypts without checking the server,
protects against eavesdropping only, and is never a default. verify-ca is not offered.
Add sslrootcert=PATH (or --database-ssl-rootcert PATH) to trust a private certificate
authority. A remote host defaults to verify-full; this machine defaults to prefer.

Advanced connection settings (--database-option, repeatable): options,
application_name, connect_timeout, target_session_attrs, channel_binding,
sslnegotiation, keepalives, keepalives_idle, keepalives_interval,
keepalives_retries, tcp_user_timeout, hostaddr, load_balance_hosts.

Encryption key (asked once, then remembered; --key-store answers it):
  file      an owner-only key file; works on any machine (recommended)
  keystore  the OS secret store; more secure, needs one to exist
Sync key (asked once and only when multi-host sync is in play; --sync-store answers it):
  file      an owner-only sync key file; share it with another node (recommended)
  keystore  the OS secret store; suits one operator on one machine
Services:
  --embed local runs the local Docker sidecar and needs no key
  --embed online needs --embed-url, --embed-model, and --embed-key, and https
  --rerank also accepts skip
  --extract online is reported and skipped; hosted extraction does not exist yet

Every prompt has a flag equivalent: non-interactive runs (piped stdin, --yes, or
--non-interactive) never prompt and fail fast when a required flag is missing.
--allow-untested saves the answers when a connection or endpoint test fails, with
a warning that Clio will not work until the failure is fixed.
The default config path is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clio/deployment.json
(fallback ~/.config/clio/deployment.json); --config overrides it and
CLIO_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG overrides the default (an empty value disables loading).

usage: clio sync key export [--output json|text]
       prints the stored key on purpose; a shell flag or environment variable leaves it in process listings, so a shared deployment should pass CLIO_SYNC_KEY_FILE pointing at an owner-only key file; this one deliberate exposure is how a rotation reaches each peer: copy the new key to every peer, confirm the fingerprints match, and rely on the rotation only then

Options:
  --output json|text  Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent.
Global flags:
  --db PATH  Overrides the store address that `db_target::resolve_target` opens; config and environment decide it when absent.
  --backend sqlite|postgres  Selects the store backend that `db_target::resolve_target` hands to the resolver; config or the address decides it when absent.
  --bank BANK  Scopes the command to one bank; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and the write scope defaults to `default`.
  --actor ACTOR  Names the acting identity; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and `auth_cli` reads it for the actor commands.
  --no-input  Refuses interactive input; `backup_restore_cli` treats a run with it as non-interactive.
  --yes  Answers yes to the destructive-confirmation gate that `cli_confirm::confirmed` applies.

usage: clio sync keygen [--store file|keystore] [--output json|text]
       creates the key in the recorded store (the recommended file store when none is recorded), records the store choice, and prints the key exactly once; it cannot be recovered except with `clio sync key export`; the key never leaves the node except through that export; generating a new key on a node that already holds one rotates: the node seals with the newest key and opens with any key it holds; a rotation is not done until every peer holds the new key — give it to each peer, confirm the fingerprint matches with `clio sync key status` on both sides, and only then rely on it; a peer that has not been given the new key dead-letters every inbound row and its pull cursor freezes until it gets one, while content sealed under a key the peer still holds stays readable

Options:
  --store file|keystore  Chooses where `sync_key_cli::keygen` writes the key via `KeySource::parse`: `file` or `keystore`; absent, the recorded choice or the recommended `file` store decides.
  --output json|text  Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent.

  --bank BANK  Scopes the command to one bank; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and the write scope defaults to `default`.
  --actor ACTOR  Names the acting identity; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and `auth_cli` reads it for the actor commands.
  --no-input  Refuses interactive input; `backup_restore_cli` treats a run with it as non-interactive.
  --yes  Answers yes to the destructive-confirmation gate that `cli_confirm::confirmed` applies.
